quickAnswer: Swallowable gastric balloons such as Allurion require a 15- to 20-minute outpatient visit without endoscopy or anesthesia and pass naturally after roughly 16 weeks, whereas endoscopic balloons stay 6 to 12 months and require sedation for placement and removal. body.text: Because intragastric balloons involve no surgical incisions, many travellers underestimate the first 48 to 72 hours of gastric cramping and nausea. At [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/about), our two founders work on a client-paid, flat-fee basis—paid by our clients and independent of provider commissions—so your Istanbul hotel, timing, and return flight are built around real recovery comfort rather than a rushed turnaround. We coordinate your visit. Your licensed medical team makes clinical decisions.
How does a swallowable balloon differ from an endoscopic gastric balloon?

A swallowable device like the [Allurion Gastric Balloon](https://www.allurion.com/en/allurion-gastric-balloon/how-it-works) is swallowed as a capsule attached to a thin catheter, verified by quick X-ray, filled with fluid during an outpatient visit under 20 minutes without endoscopy or anesthesia, and designed to deflate and pass naturally at about 16 weeks. Endoscopic balloons (such as 6-month or 12-month saline-filled systems) require light sedation and gastroscopy for both placement and later removal.

body.text: Clinical overviews from [NCBI StatPearls on intragastric balloons](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK578184/) and [Allurion clinical results](https://www.allurion.com/en/results) show that most weight reduction happens in the first three to four months as the balloon slows gastric emptying and reinforces smaller portions.
How many days in Istanbul are needed for placement and nausea monitoring?

Plan 3 to 4 nights in Istanbul even for a 20-minute swallowable placement. As the [Mayo Clinic intragastric balloon guide](https://www.mayoclinic.org/tests-procedures/intragastric-balloon/about/pac-20394435) notes, nausea, vomiting, and abdominal cramping affect roughly one-third of patients during the first few days after insertion, and boarding a flight while unable to keep fluids down risks severe dehydration.
A realistic 4-day rhythm avoids flying during peak adjustment symptoms:

items: Day 1: Arrive in Istanbul, settle into a quiet hotel close to your clinic, and complete fasting instructions.
Day 2: Pre-procedure assessment, balloon placement, initial observation, and prescribed anti-nausea and acid-suppression medications.
Day 3: Hotel rest with small sips of water and electrolytes; clinic check-in or IV hydration at the hospital if nausea persists.
Day 4: Brief medical clearance check confirming oral hydration tolerance, followed by private airport transfer home.

body.text: What nutritional follow-up is required after returning home?

A gastric balloon is a temporary tool, not a standalone fix—long-term weight maintenance depends on structured dietitian coaching as you progress from clear liquids to purees, soft foods, and balanced solid meals. Before travelling, confirm how your provider delivers remote dietitian check-ins and connected-scale tracking over the 4 to 12 months after placement, and inform your home GP so you have local clinical backup if symptoms arise.

Also know the red-flag symptoms highlighted in the [FDA alert on liquid-filled intragastric balloons](https://www.fda.gov/medical-devices/letters-health-care-providers/fda-alerts-health-care-providers-about-potential-risks-liquid-filled-intragastric-balloons): persistent severe abdominal or back pain, marked abdominal swelling, or unrelenting vomiting require urgent medical evaluation to rule out rare complications such as spontaneous over-inflation, ulceration, or acute pancreatitis.

In 2026, realistic pricing at licensed Istanbul hospitals and gastroenterology centers typically runs €1,700 to €2,600 for 6-month endoscopic saline balloons, €2,400 to €3,000 for the swallowable Allurion program, and €2,800 to €3,500 for 12-month adjustable or extended-duration endoscopic balloons. Always verify whether endoscopic removal fees, IV hydration rescue visits, and remote dietitian sessions are included or billed separately.

faq.q: Can I fly home the same evening after a swallowable gastric balloon?
faq.a: Same-day flying is strongly discouraged. Cramping and nausea often start 4 to 8 hours after placement, making a 3- to 4-night Istanbul stay far safer and more comfortable.

faq.q: Where do I get an endoscopic gastric balloon removed if I live outside Türkiye?
faq.a: You can either return to Istanbul for a short 2-night removal trip or arrange endoscopic removal with a private gastroenterologist in your home country—confirm local removal pricing before choosing an endoscopic model.

faq.q: What BMI range is typically evaluated for a gastric balloon?
faq.a: Clinicians commonly evaluate intragastric balloons for adults with a BMI of roughly 27 to 35+ who want a non-surgical option or a bridge before other treatments, subject to full medical screening.

faq.q: What if I cannot tolerate the balloon during the first week?
faq.a: Most patients settle within 3 to 5 days with prescribed anti-emetics and acid blockers. In rare intolerance cases, a gastroenterologist can deflate and remove the balloon endoscopically.

faq.q: Can I sightsee in Istanbul right after gastric balloon placement?
faq.a: Keep days 2 and 3 completely unscheduled for hotel rest. If you want light sightseeing or Bosphorus dining, schedule it before placement day rather than afterward.
